newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak blue chips mixed, SAX off 0.38pts to 212.56.
newsitem.headline: Slovak blue chips mixed, SAX off 0.38pts to 212.56.

text.p: Leading Slovak shares closed mixed on the Bratislava Stock Exchange on Friday to end a listless week, with the 12-share SAX index slipping 0.38 points to 212.56.
Slovak crude oil refiner Slovnaft, the most heavily- weighted issue on the index, did not trade, while gas storage firm Nafta closed up 50 crowns at 2,100.
Brokers noted that while "the few final deals" in Nafta near the closing price within a 2,100-2,150 crown range, some 10,000 share blocks were available for as little as 1,950 crowns.
"Generally, the interest in our market has dampened on the recent examples of the privatisation practics, the one of Nafta has a negative affect on the market," said Peter Krutil of Creditanstalt.

Added Libor Chrast of ING Barings: "The Nafta increase is only optical, a selling mood has casted over it, but the interest to buy it is not furious. I have the feeling someone is trying only to prop it up."
Steel maker VSZ closed down seven crowns at 646, while bank VUB rose 45 crowns at 1,895 and pharmaceutical maker Biotika gained crowns at 1,000.
Overall volume boosted mainly by direct tradaes climbed to 945,865 shares traded from 178,583 shares on Thursday, as turnover rose to 502.3 million crowns from 249.49 million.
